annual_volume_notes: Handles approximately 12-15% of global maritime trade and ~30% of global container ship traffic, linking the Mediterranean to the Red Sea.
typical_disruption_causes: Vessel groundings and waterway blockages
Geopolitical conflicts and regional missile threats
Canal authority toll tariff disputes
Sandstorms causing low visibility and strong winds

annual_volume_notes: Primary sea route connecting the Indian and Pacific Oceans; over 85,000 vessels transit annually, representing roughly 25% of global traded merchandise.
typical_disruption_causes: Piracy, armed robbery, and maritime crime
Severe haze and smog from regional seasonal fires reducing visibility
Collisions and grounding risks in narrow, shallow channels (e.g., Phillips Channel)
Vessel traffic congestion

annual_volume_notes: Transits around 5% of global maritime commerce, connecting Atlantic and Pacific Oceans; vital corridor for US Gulf Coast exports to Asia.
typical_disruption_causes: Drought and freshwater deficits in Gatun Lake restricting draft depths and daily slots
Bottlenecks and extended waiting times for non-booked vessels
Maintenance lock outages and operational restrictions

annual_volume_notes: The world's most critical petroleum transit chokepoint; processes over 20-21 million barrels of oil per day (roughly 20-25% of global petroleum consumption).
typical_disruption_causes: Military conflicts and geopolitical skirmishes
State-sponsored vessel seizures and naval harassment
Naval mines and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) strikes
Electronic navigation interference and GPS spoofing

annual_volume_notes: Crucial gatekeeper to the southern Red Sea and Suez Canal, carrying approximately 6.2 million barrels per day of crude and refined petroleum along with high container volumes.
typical_disruption_causes: Missile, drone, and waterborne explosive attacks by regional non-state actors
Regional warfare spillover
Commercial fleet diversions around Africa leading to route desertion

annual_volume_notes: The world's busiest container port for over a decade, handling upwards of 47 million TEUs annually.
typical_disruption_causes: Severe typhoons and summer storm surges in the Yangtze River delta
Epidemic quarantine restrictions and port worker shortages
Terminal yard congestion and container chassis deficits
Customs inspection backlogs

annual_volume_notes: World's top container transshipment port and largest marine bunkering hub, processing over 38-39 million TEUs per year.
typical_disruption_causes: Upstream schedule disruptions cascading into intense yard storage pileups
Bunker fuel supply contamination scares
Monsoonal squalls and adverse maritime sea states

annual_volume_notes: Largest seaport in Europe, handling roughly 440 million metric tons of goods and over 14 million TEUs each year.
typical_disruption_causes: Labor strikes and dockworker wage disputes
Low water levels on the River Rhine preventing inland barge transport
Severe North Sea gales and tidal surges
Customs bottlenecks and terminal IT/cyber incidents

annual_volume_notes: Primary maritime gateway for US-transpacific container trade, handling 9-10 million TEUs individually and nearly 19 million TEUs combined with Long Beach.
typical_disruption_causes: Longshoremen union contract negotiation impasses and labor slowdowns
Shortages of intermodal truck chassis and railcar availability
Seasonal import peak volume spikes leading to anchorage queues
Stricter environmental clean-truck and emissions mandate transitions

annual_volume_notes: Europe's second-largest container port and host to Europe's largest petrochemical cluster, processing over 270-290 million tons of cargo annually.
typical_disruption_causes: National and port-specific general strikes
Navigation restrictions and tidal limitations on the Western Scheldt river
Environmental regulations impacting inland transportation

product_categories: Raw Steel, Pig Iron & Scrap Metal
annual_volume_notes: Crucial corridor linking the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara and Mediterranean; over 40,000 vessels transit annually, crucial for global food security.
typical_disruption_causes: Regional warfare in the Black Sea (naval mines, embargoes, weaponized blockades)
Narrow channels and tricky currents causing vessel engine failure groundings
Dense fog and adverse weather forcing one-way or suspended transit
Turkish maritime regulation and escort requirements

route_name: Cape of Good Hope Sea Route
region: Sub-Saharan Africa / South Atlantic & Indian Ocean
product_categories: Crude Oil & Refined Products on VLCCs
annual_volume_notes: Major alternative maritime route bypass whenever Suez or Red Sea transits face hazards; extends Asia-Europe transit by 10-14 days.
typical_disruption_causes: Severe Southern Ocean winter storms, high swells, and rogue waves
Lack of nearby deep-water bunkering, refueling, and ship repair hubs
Bunker fuel cost spikes due to longer sailing distance

annual_volume_notes: Sixth busiest container port in the world and key Northeast Asian transshipment center, handling over 22 million TEUs annually.
typical_disruption_causes: Summer and autumn typhoons causing maritime shutdowns
Domestic unionized trucker walkouts and logistics strikes
Geopolitical and security tensions in the surrounding East Asian seas

product_categories: Fresh Agricultural Produce from North Africa & Mediterranean
annual_volume_notes: Critical narrow waterway connecting the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean Sea, accommodating over 100,000 vessel movements per year.
typical_disruption_causes: Intense naval and merchant traffic congestion causing collision hazards
Heavy easterly gales ('Levante') and thick fog banks
Localized marine mammal interactions causing rudder damage to smaller vessels
Coastguard interdiction and customs inspection delays
